attempts.summary: On node1, limited datauser to 100MB under /srv/data using XFS project quota, enforced by the filesystem itself. Root fs (/dev/vda3, XFS) needed prjquota enabled, which required adding rootflags=pquota via grubby and /etc/fstab plus a reboot (XFS quota accounting can only be enabled at initial mount, live remount does not work). Project "datauser" (id 1000) is bound to /srv/data with bhard=bsoft=100M. Verified enforcement: writes up to 100MB succeed; further writes fail with ENOSPC at exactly 100M used, both before and after the node restart. Completed the mandatory single-node restart-evidence protocol: baseline boot_id captured, background reboot acknowledged, node polled back up, new boot_id confirmed, and /srv/data + datauser + quota config verified intact and still enforcing post-reboot.
